schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workload_table (id INT PRIMARY KEY, category VARCHAR(64), payload NVARCHAR(MAX), created_at DATETIME);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS resource_intensive_table (id INT PRIMARY KEY, data NVARCHAR(MAX), ref_id INT, FOREIGN KEY (ref_id) REFERENCES workload_table(id));
generation_sql: INSERT INTO workload_table (id, category, payload, created_at) SELECT n, CASE WHEN n % 10 = 0 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END, REPLICATE('A', 1000), GETDATE() FROM (SELECT TOP {row_count} ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)) AS n FROM sys.objects) AS numbers;
INSERT INTO resource_intensive_table (id, data, ref_id) SELECT n, REPLICATE('B', 2000), n FROM (SELECT TOP {row_count} ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)) AS n FROM sys.objects) AS numbers;

tables.name: workload_table
tables.purpose: Simulates the main workload driving memory grants and parallelism.
tables.distribution_notes: Skewed distribution with 'high' category being less frequent.

tables.name: resource_intensive_table
tables.purpose: Simulates resource-intensive operations with large payloads.

calibration_queries.sql: SELECT w.id, r.data FROM workload_table w JOIN resource_intensive_table r ON w.id = r.ref_id WHERE w.category = 'high' ORDER BY w.created_at DESC;
calibration_queries.objective: Verify that the query generates high memory grants and parallel execution plans.
expected_evidence: The plan shows parallelism operators (e.g., Parallelism, Gather Streams).
The query requests significant memory grants.
RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE waits are observed during execution.
